Liquidity by strike — why the default stops at six strikes in

Share of the exit day’s one-minute bars in which the contract did not trade at all (high equals low). In such a minute the worst-fill rule has no low to punish, so a deeper strike’s better numbers are partly untradeable.

    The optional filters, and exactly how each one is calculated
      The exit, next session
      What this rule does not calculate, and why
      No volatility, no trend, no moving average, no range ratio, no momentum, no filter on the size of the day’s move, no lookback of any length. The only time frame is the one-minute candle, used to build the daily bar and to price the exit minute by minute. Each of v1’s seven features and fourteen other filters were measured on this data before v2 was fixed: none raised the win rate on both the six months and the five years, and a minimum move size lowered it. The exit rule and the strike depth are the two things that moved the result, so they are the two things this rule sets.
